MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JANUARY 6, 2025

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

VICE CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Nicklas, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

Director Naughton thanked CHAIR MEDAWAR for his exceptional service and leadership and for
guiding thoughtful discussions on challenging issues and projects that came before the Planning
Commission in 2024.

Director Naughton stated that VICE CHAIR OLSON will be the Planning Commission Chair and
COMMISSIONER NICKLAS will be the Planning Commission Vice Chair.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, made a motion seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF DECEMBER 2,
  2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

B.  2024 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JUNE 1, 2024 - DECEMBER 31, 2024

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the age of some of the cases in the code compliance
report, especially those that are for work requiring permits. Director Naughton explained that it is
not uncommon for some cases to extend many years due to litigation or other issues.

CHAIR OLSON inquired about a case that was originally opened in 2018 and later looked into
again in 2022. Director Naughton explained that projects have different timelines. If, for example,
a project goes to plan check they have a longer timeline to submit revisions to address corrections,

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 6, 2025
  1
 and once a permit is issued, they have a year to call for a first inspection. Projects remain open
until they receive a final inspection.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked what percentage of cases that require permits
obtain permits. Director Naughton stated that it’s 100%; however, some cases may take from
weeks to years to get to that point.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if any structures have been required to be removed.
Director Naughton stated that there is an existing case where a structure was required to be
removed and is being relocated to another location on the property.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about structures that cross property lines. Director
Naughton stated that structures that cross property lines are required to be removed or may apply
for an easement. However, it is difficult for neighbors to want to grant an easement on their
property.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  APPROVE ITEM 7A AND 7B

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240472; ADDRESS: 550 Deep Valley Drive, Suite
  116, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Mega Looma LLC; A request for a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240473) to allow an indoor amusement/entertainment
  facility that includes a snack bar for the sale of packaged foods, soft drinks, beer and wine
  within the Promenade PV shopping center.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240472. The proposal includes the operation of a 34,230 SF indoor
amusement/entertainment facility and will include a snack bar with packaged foods, soft drinks,
beer and wine. They will be open from 11 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday, and 11
a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Friday through Sunday. Assistant Kawagoe provided floor plans for each of
the two levels, which detailed the way that the facility will be configured.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that the proposed project meets Conditional Use Permit
findings and complies with the applicable development standards for the CGMU district.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and, adopt
Resolution No. PA-240472, approving the project, and in accordance with CEQA determine that
the project is Categorically Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301 - Existing Facilities.

PUBLIC HEARING OPENED

Cynthia Hu, Promenade PV, stated that their intent with Mega Looma is to turn Palos Verdes into
a community center and stated that she believes that the majority of Palos Verdes is family-
oriented, and they would like to bring the community together through fun, while providing a safe
environment for kids.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Ms. Hu stated that Mega
Looma is a separate company from the mall.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that a similar entertainment facility was approved at the
mall and asked if this is in addition to that proposal. Ms. Hu stated that this is in addition to the
bowling alley that was proposed.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about the timeline for the bowling alley. Ms. Hu
stated that it should be approximately twelve months. Mega Looma should be open in December
2025.

Gloria Lee, stated that she is the owner of Looma Space which is on Palos Verdes Drive North

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 6, 2025
  2
 and is for kids six and under and will be celebrating its two-year anniversary next month. She
explained that Looma Space was created when her kids were younger and now that they are
older, the idea for Mega Looma came about. She stated that other locations were considered but
she believes that the South Bay needs a space like this. She further stated that she receives
requests from the nearby school districts and daycares for field trips and having a space in the
South Bay is ideal.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240472 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: OLSON, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, MEDAWAR,
NOES:
ABSENT: NICKLAS, YOO
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240472,  a Conditional  Use  Permit  (CUP-240473)  to allow  an  indoor
amusement/entertainment facility that includes a snack bar for the sale of packaged foods, soft
drinks, beer and wine within the Promenade PV shopping center. There is a 20-day appeal period
by which any member of the public or the City Council by its own motion may appeal this project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240536; ADDRESS: 550 Deep Valley Drive, Suite 167,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Kanako Nishikawa, Kiddleton Inc.; A request
  for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240537) to allow an arcade use in Unit 167 at the
  Promenade PV shopping center.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240536. The proposal is for the operation of an arcade that includes mini
crane or claw machine arcade games, and character card battle machines with a total of 26
arcade games in this location. The business plan indicates that the arcade would operate seven
days a week between 11:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. One employee would be on site to open the
facility from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. and to close in the evening between 6:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m.,
which means that there would be no staff on site between 2:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the required Conditional Use Permit findings can be made for
this project and the project meets the applicable development standards for the CGMU district.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the public
hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and, adopt Resolution
No. PA-240536, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked for clarification regarding the business being unstaffed
from 2:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. Senior Planner Berry stated it is her understanding per conversations
with the applicant that this business does not require on-site management of the games.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that public restrooms are not shown on the plan and
asked how far the mall restrooms are from this site. Senior Planner Berry stated that the
employees and customers will need to use the public restrooms in the mall which are less than
500 FT from the site.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked mall ownership if there will be additional security for the
increasing number of businesses coming to the mall.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 6, 2025
  3
 Cynthia Hu, Promenade PV, stated that a public restroom will be added to a more centralized
location of the mall. Additional lighting, cameras, and security on-site, both in the number of hours
and the number of people will be added. She stated that it is important to keep the site safe. She
added that they have worked with the Lomita Sheriff to review their security plan and they have
also monitored their security system.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Ms. Hu stated that Dilly D’s
will be across from this business and nearby are Sky Photo, Ramen, and Boba. She stated that
the goal with this business is to have a place for all age groups that will be open all day. Ms. Hu
stated that with the mall security alone should suffice for these businesses.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if Transition to Independence is still a tenant. Ms.
Hu stated that they are still a tenant and have been relocated to another location within the mall.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER expressed his concern with there being no staff during certain
hours of the day.

CHAIR OLSON added that the hours from 2:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. would be a high traffic time since
this is when Junior and High School students are out of school.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that security cannot be at this location at all times
and asked if there is a way to post signs where people could call for issues or to call for security.
Ms. Hu stated that she would be amenable to having prominent signs posted inside the unit with
a phone number to call for any issues.

Kanaka Nishikawa, representing Kiddleton, stated that he will hire staff to cover the hours from
2:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. and stated that he will also be installing six or seven security cameras in
the unit. He also stated that QR codes will be placed on the machines for customers to use in
case there are any issues with the machines.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR explained that he understands that with advances in technology
there are now businesses that do not require employees to be present; however, the City is not
there yet and requested that the applicant reconsider and have staff present during business
hours.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Mr. Nishikawa stated that
they operate 500 of these businesses nationwide and about 100 in California. Tenant spaces,
such as the one being proposed, can be found at Tokyo Central in Gardena and Westfield in
Culver City.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER
to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240536 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL CONDITION THAT STAFF
  BE PRESENT DURING ALL BUSINESS HOURS.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that this business is simple and that the mall
security may be sufficient. She suggested beginning with adding a condition of approval for
signage with a phone number to reach security for any issues that may arise. She also added that
they are required to maintain a log of any calls to security, the Sheriff’s, or complaints to the City;
if there occur within a twelve-month period, then the applicant return to the Planning Commission
to determine if the business should be required to have full-time staff.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR suggested changing the hours of when staff is in the business to
the more high traffic time between 2:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 6, 2025
  4
 A brief discussion ensued.

Ms. Hu stated that the applicant has agreed to have staff at the business full-time.

COMMISSIONER  ROMANELLI  restated  the  motion,  seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240536 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL CONDITION THAT STAFF
  BE PRESENT DURING ALL BUSINESS HOURS.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES:
ABSENT: NICKLAS, YOO
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240536, a request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240537) to allow an arcade use in Unit
167 at the Promenade PV shopping center. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member
of the public or the City Council by its own motion may appeal the project.

10.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that a customer of his mentioned that when travelling on
Silver Spur going west towards the high school, there are two lanes that merge; however, the sign
says, “left lane ends”. Director Naughton stated that she will need to make sure that it is in Rolling
Hills Estates’ jurisdiction and will bring it to the Public Work Directors attention.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there could be a request for the “No Tun on Red”
sign on PVDN/PVDE be reconsidered and stated that the sign does not seem to be necessary.
Director Naughton stated that she will bring it to the Public Works Directors attention.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there are any businesses that do not have staff on-site.
Director Naughton stated that there are not; however, there are no other business with a similar
business model to the one proposed (by Kiddleton).

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the back lot (at 758 Silver Spur Road) still has not been
cleaned up and asked for a follow-up. Director Naughton stated that staff have a meeting
scheduled with the property owner at the end of the week.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about the status of the George F Canyon Nature
Center. Director Naughton stated that the project is currently on hold due to funding issues due
to the increased cost of construction. COMMISSIONER OLSON questioned the shortfall amount.
Director Naughton stated that she can bring this information to the next Planning Commission
meeting.

11.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A.  2025 COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS-
  Environmental Advisory Committee (2024: Repp-Loadsman)
  Equestrian Committee (2024: Romanelli)
  Traffic and Safety Committee (2024: Olson)

 The PLANNING COMMISSIONERS continue representing the same committees.

B.  Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commissioner’s Academy will be held in Santa
  Rosa on March 5-7, 2025. If anyone would like to attend, please let staff know.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, NOVEMBER 12, 2024

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 11A.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 6, 2025
  5
 There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR OLSON adjourned the meeting at 7:59 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, February 3, 2025 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045
Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Larry Olson, Chair
